CONFIRM C0031 | FIND: `_count_tool_issues()` returns `0` on any runner exception, which makes fix evaluation treat tool failure as “no issues”. In `evaluate_fix()`, all pre/post counts come through `_count_tool_issues`; if pyright/ruff/bandit crashes on the patched file, `new_*` becomes 0. `_compute_fix_verdict()` then sees non-positive net counts and can label the fix SAFE/NEUTRAL. FOLLOW: this crosses the interface into the immune pipeline Stage 4, where `evaluate_fixes()` marks findings `verified=True` for SAFE/NEUTRAL verdicts. That can falsely close bugs and activate NK’s bug-closed dedup gate on later rounds. FIX: tool execution failure in `_count_tool_issues()` must not map to 0; return an explicit failure signal or a penalty count that forces HARMFUL/UNEVALUABLE.

CONFIRM C0028 | FIND: `run_mypy()` parses plain-text mypy output with a single-line regex. Mypy commonly emits wrapped diagnostics and related `note:` lines; those are either dropped or mis-associated. FOLLOW: health scan undercounts diagnostics, and fix evaluation baselines/post-fix counts from mypy are unreliable wherever mypy emits nontrivial output. That degrades both inter-round health signals and any future use of mypy counts for gating. FIX: prefer structured mypy output and parse that mechanically; only fall back to text parsing if JSON is unavailable.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox imports or multi-file context; it writes only the patched target file into a tempdir, then runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that lone file path. For fixes in `endocrine.py`, both pyright and import-resolving tools depend on package context (`from bench.dm._types import Finding`). In the tempdir there is no `bench/` package, so post-fix analysis is not evaluating the fix against the real project context. Evidence: `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))` and the subsequent `_count_tool_issues(..., patched_path)` calls operate on a standalone file, not a sandboxed copy of the repo tree.
FOLLOW: This breaks the core “sandbox-test proposed fixes” feature. A harmless fix can be marked HARMFUL because imports fail in isolation; a harmful fix that only breaks project integration can be marked SAFE because cross-file dependencies are absent. That propagates into `evaluate_fixes()`, then into `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` Stage 4 where SAFE/NEUTRAL results set `finding.verified = True`, which can prematurely close findings and suppress rediscovery through NK dedup.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — copy the minimal project context into the tempdir before analysis: preserve the target file’s relative repo path and also copy the `bench/` package subtree needed for imports, then run the tools from the tempdir against that sandboxed path.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.89
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: FIND — test execution in `evaluate_fix()` is not actually bound to the patched sandbox content. The code runs `_run_tool(test_cmd, cwd=tmpdir)`, but `test_cmd` is passed through unchanged. In context, the immune pipeline supplies `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", "-x", "-q", "--tb=no", "--no-header", "-q"]`. Because only one patched file is copied into `tmpdir` and no sandboxed `bench/tests/` tree or adjusted paths are created, pytest either targets a non-existent path in the tempdir or resolves imports/tests against the original checkout via interpreter path semantics, not the patched sandbox.
FOLLOW: The advertised guarantee “Fix evaluation is sandboxed (tempdir, never modifies actual source)” is false in practice for tests. Tests may fail spuriously because the test tree is missing, or pass while exercising the unpatched source tree. That yields wrong SAFE/HARMFUL verdicts, and those wrong verdicts feed directly into immune Stage 4 verification and downstream bug closure.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when `test_cmd` is provided, copy the referenced test tree plus required package tree into the tempdir and rewrite the command to point at sandbox-relative paths before execution.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can select the wrong source file by substring containment. It returns a match when `sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. A filename fragment mentioned in a description/proposed fix can match unrelated paths sharing that substring. Evidence: the fallback logic does not require path-component equality, basename equality, or uniqueness; it accepts any containment hit.
FOLLOW: Fix evaluation can patch and analyze the wrong file while still returning a concrete verdict. That is silently wrong, not just unevaluable: pre/post tool counts come from the wrong file, tests may not exercise the intended bug, and the immune pipeline may mark the original finding verified based on evidence from an unrelated source file.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — resolve target files by exact absolute-path match first, then unique basename match among `source_paths`; if resolution is ambiguous, return `None` and mark the fix UNEVALUABLE.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.78
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.48
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` collapses all tool deltas into one signed sum: `total_net = net_type + net_ruff + net_bandit`. That lets regressions in one tool be cancelled by improvements in another. Example from the code path: +1 new Bandit issue and -1 Ruff issue gives `total_net == 0`, so the fix can be NEUTRAL or SAFE if tests pass.
FOLLOW: This is silently wrong fix evaluation. Security regressions or new type errors can be masked by lint cleanup, producing SAFE/NEUTRAL verdicts for harmful fixes. Those verdicts are then consumed by the immune pipeline, where NEUTRAL is sufficient to mark a finding verified and close the bug.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — classify as HARMFUL if any individual net metric is positive; only use aggregate reduction to decide SAFE after confirming no per-tool regression.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.73
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.37
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the advertised “defect detection” categories do not actually include dead-code detection from type checkers/linters beyond coarse pyright/ruff heuristics, and `scan_health()` never invokes any classifier over the aggregated diagnostics despite the module contract claiming a separate capability “Defect detection — classify findings by defect category”. In implementation there is no standalone defect-detection function; categorisation only happens incidentally inside individual runners.
FOLLOW: This feature boundary matters to `insect_brain`, which receives a `HealthScan` as if the endocrine layer has performed a complete classification stage. Missing categories and the absence of a dedicated pass mean some promised signals never fire, reducing the usefulness of health data for pacing/decision logic and misleading human reviewers about what the endocrine layer actually checked.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — make the contract honest for the PoC: remove the standalone “Defect detection” capability claim from the module/class docstrings and describe categorisation as best-effort tagging attached to tool diagnostics.
VERIFIED: TRUE
